data.narrative:
Epsilon3, a Space & Aerospace company founded by Laura Crabtree and Max Mednik, is a Series A-stage venture that has raised $19M to date. The valuation universe includes 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers spanning the sector, though a tight cohort of same-stage, similar-tier companies remains limited.

The analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement to the $19M total raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $38M. Peer-median triangulation is not applicable: while 11 same-sector peers exist, fewer than three datapoints satisfy the narrow filters of same-stage, adjacent-stage, or comparable valuation tier. Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied because target revenue is not disclosed, precluding P/S multiple application despite a 23.9x median P/S across the six public Space & Aerospace comps.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $32M to $44M, with a median point estimate of $38M. This range incorporates typical step-up variance but carries meaningful uncertainty. The primary constraint is data scarcity: with only one applied method, the triangulation lacks the robustness of a multi-method consensus. Revenue disclosure or access to a tighter private peer set would materially strengthen conviction. Early-stage space companies exhibit wide dispersion in stage-to-stage multiples; Epsilon3's specific technology, market traction, and capital efficiency relative to peers warrant detailed diligence beyond valuation mechanics.
